summary: Locked the visual direction from TASK-009 and refactored its implementation into a reusable production-scene architecture, without rendering the full video. Inspected create_character_proof.py (TASK-009) and found its cross-fade timing, transition sweep, glow pass, and character-safety logic duplicated inside each of its 6 beat functions. Extracted that into src/scene_engine.py: a Scene dataclass implementing the task's 9-field contract (metadata, narration segment, character placement, background/stage, diagram layer, object animation, camera, transition, timing/validation) and render_scenes(), a single runner that turns a list of Scenes into a draw_frame function. create_character_proof.py's 6 beats were converted into Scene entries (SCENES list) with the same draw_diagram content as before -- no new visuals, no redesigned character, only the surrounding plumbing changed. While converting, found and fixed a real regression: TASK-009 composited its TAKEAWAY character as a special case in addition to whichever beat's character was still fading out, causing two poses to render superimposed for about 0.5s at the SCALE-to-TAKEAWAY boundary. On the engine, TAKEAWAY is just the last Scene in the list, so its character naturally replaces the previous one once its own alpha is non-zero -- confirmed fixed by rendering the same timestamp (t=50.7s) before and after the refactor. Documented the locked visual direction, the character's usable poses (and why 'reference' stays excluded), and the scene contract in docs/visual_system.md, including an explicitly-named gap (narration is still one flat script file, not yet stitched from per-scene segments) as the natural next architectural step before the full multi-minute video.

next_action: Per TASK-010's stop condition, halting here -- not starting the full 2-3 minute video, awaiting the next task. The architecture now supports adding remaining full-video scenes as Scene entries without duplicating rendering logic. Two things worth deciding before that build starts: (1) the narration-wiring gap named in docs/visual_system.md (per-scene narration segments vs. one flat script), and (2) whether the earlier non-character visual directions (TASK-005 dark theme, TASK-006 light theme without character) should be formally retired now that TASK-010 has locked this character-led direction as canonical, so the repo doesn't keep carrying three unconverged styles.
